request: Analyze GSE178262 for PMID 34142717 (Transcriptomic, proteomic and phosphoproteomic underpinnings of daily exercise performance and zeitgeber activity of training in mouse muscle.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.primary_estimand: Effect of an acute bout of high-intensity treadmill exercise (sacrificed 0 h or 3 h after exhaustion, started at ZT0 or ZT12) on quadriceps gene expression versus time-of-sacrifice-matched sedentary mice; secondary: daytime versus night-time voluntary wheel-running training (DA vs CTRL) in gastrocnemius at ZT4 and ZT16.
planned_contrasts: Ex+0h ZT0 vs Sed ZT0 (S3.3.p2; Fig 5A)
Ex+3h ZT0 vs Sed ZT4 (FIG2 legend: Sed ZT4 is the 3 h control; Fig 5B)
DA vs CTRL at ZT4: 2094 DEGs (S3.8.p1; Fig 12A)
CTRL vs DA at ZT16: 368 DEGs (S3.8.p1; Fig 12A)
final.paper_method: kallisto -> tximport lengthScaledTPM gene pseudo-counts -> DESeq2 1.26.0, shrunken LFC (S2.8.p2); DEGs FDR <= 0.05 (S3.3.p2)
final.sample_inclusion: RNA-seq of quadriceps (treadmill, n=3/group) and gastrocnemius (wheel, n=4/group); 40 samples, each sequenced on two lanes of the same library

paper_results.treadmill: Venn counts only in Fig 5A/B and Supp Table 1 (not in text); ~25% of DEGs shared between ZT0 and ZT12

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: S3.3.p1-p2: RNA-seq at ZT0 and ZT12 acute treadmill exercise vs sedentary, DEGs FDR<=0.05. S3.8.p1: DA vs CTRL wheel DEG counts. S2.3.p1: the wheel contrast is day- versus night-time training; sedentary vs wheel is explicitly out of scope. The FIG2 legend fixes the sedentary control as matched to the time of sacrifice.

checks: GSE178262 data_processing restates the paper's kallisto/tximport/DESeq2 methods (S2.8.p2)
sample titles Sed/Ex +0h/Ex +3h/CTRL/DA at ZT0/4/12/16 match the paper design
contact is the Handschin lab, Biozentrum Basel

ownership.reasoning: S2.8.p2 method text is reproduced in GEO data_processing; sample labels mirror the Fig 5 and Fig 12 designs.

alignment.reasoning: The deposited matrix has 80 lane columns (L001/L002 of one library per sample; GEO description says same library). prep/merge_lanes.py sums the two lanes of each sample (paired by the sample number S<n> present in both the column name and the GSM description) and renames to GSM ids, so alignment is exact on the metadata index. grp = title treatment + ZT; tissue = source_name_ch1 (tissue is fully nested in experiment).

matrix.reasoning: Non-integer tximport lengthScaledTPM gene-level pseudo-counts (data_processing; integer fraction 0.30 before lane summing), the same input as the paper's DESeq2 (S2.8.p2). Rounded for pydeseq2. Row IDs are Entrez gene IDs.

design.reasoning: Independent animals per group (n=3 treadmill, n=4 wheel). Six pairwise contrasts, each a separate two-group fit within its tissue. Treadmill: acute exercise vs sedentary mice sacrificed at the matched ZT (FIG2 legend). Wheel: the paper compares day vs night-time wheel activity at the ZT where each group runs (S3.8.p1), not sedentary vs wheel (S2.3.p1), so it is a training-timing contrast.

candidates.reason_rejected: circadian phase confounded; paper stratifies by ZT and sacrifice time
no wheel-free sedentary group in the gastrocnemius set; paper excludes it (S2.3.p1)

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals; no litter or batch column. Lane replicates are summed per library so no pseudo-replication. Tissue is nested in experiment and handled by subsetting.

deviations: LFC not shrunk (does not change padj)
two-group fit per contrast; paper's exact model formula not stated

method.reasoning: Estimated counts; DESeq2 is the paper's method (S2.8.p2). Rounded pseudo-counts are the documented route for estimated counts.

threshold.reasoning: S3.3.p2: DEGs FDR <= 0.05, no fold-change cutoff. The wheel section gives no rule; the same FDR rule is assumed. Audit: add |log2FC| > log2(1.5) as a labelled stricter comparison.

caveats: treadmill DEG counts only in Venn diagrams (not in text)
wheel contrast is day-vs-night training timing, not exercise vs sedentary
DA mice are also under time-restricted wheel and food access (S2.3.p1)
n=3 (treadmill) and n=4 (wheel) per arm: low power
Entrez IDs: enrichment and runner gene lookups not run

study.reasoning: Planned contrasts and threshold taken from the paper; gene-level lookups skipped because the matrix is keyed by Entrez IDs.
